title: God approaches you everyday
theme: The heavens declare God's immeasurable glory, yet He allows us to encounter His magnificence gently, one day and one night at a time.
opening: God's glory is inexhaustible, but His approach is gentle—and we have been given the extraordinary privilege of witnessing it.
prayer: Most holy Apostle St. Jude, faithful servant and friend of Jesus, I turn to you with trust and devotion.  Intercede for me before our Lord, that I may remain open to the wonder of His creation and never lose sight of His gentle presence.  When His magnificence exceeds my understanding, help me rest in faith rather than demand an answer. When I am distracted by the concerns of life, pray that I may recognize the quiet ways He draws near.  St. Jude, patron of difficult and seemingly hopeless causes, carry my petitions before God. Help me trust in His wisdom, His mercy, and His timing, even when I cannot see what lies ahead.  May I never take for granted the extraordinary gift of being here to witness His handiwork.
body:
“The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims his handiwork. Day pours out the word to day, and night to night imparts knowledge.” — Psalm 19:2–3

There is something extraordinary happening in these words, something I feel we have barely begun to understand.

The heavens are declaring. The sky is proclaiming. Day pours forth its message, and night imparts knowledge. This is not a single announcement, but a continuous unfolding that began long before we existed and will continue whether we are here to witness it or not.

And yet God has placed us within it.

Each day is unlike any day that has ever existed. Each night is equally new. The sun rises upon a world that has changed, however imperceptibly, and darkness reveals heavens that were present all along, hidden from our sight.

What are the heavens declaring today that they did not declare yesterday? What knowledge does this night hold that the last did not?

Perhaps the message itself is inexhaustible. God's glory cannot be contained within a single sunrise, a single night, or even a lifetime of watching the heavens. Creation continues to unfold, revealing something of its Creator without ever exhausting His magnificence.

And perhaps what moves me most is how lightly God approaches us.

The enormity of His glory is beyond anything we could comprehend. Yet He does not confront us with all of it at once. Instead, He gives us the gradual arrival of morning, the soft departure of daylight, and the quiet unveiling of the stars.

At dawn and dusk, we stand at the meeting of two revelations. One recedes as another becomes visible. Nothing has stopped. Nothing has disappeared from God's creation. We are simply being allowed to witness another part of it.

Perhaps these moments are small openings into something immeasurably greater—a gentle invitation to participate in what has always been happening.

We did not begin this proclamation. We cannot contain it, and we may never fully understand it.

But God has given us a place within it.

And every morning, every evening, He approaches us again.
